guide.prompt:
Create one 2 by 2 expression sprite sheet for the exact red fox in the reference. The reference is the approved character design, not a pose to copy full-body. Show the same head and upper chest four times, each at the same gentle three-quarter angle facing right. Preserve russet coat, creamy muzzle and chest, dark ear backs, natural fox face, delicate translucent watercolor, lighting and personality. This is for Microverse, a charming storybook ecology game.
Square image divided invisibly into four equal square cells. Put exactly one complete head-and-upper-chest portrait in each cell. All four portraits have identical size, head position, eye line, and shoulder line within their cells. Keep every ear, whisker and chest edge inside its cell with at least 8 percent empty margin on every side. No portrait touches another or the image edge. Do not draw a grid.
Reading order: top-left attentive friendly eyes open mouth closed; top-right the identical face with eyes gently closed in a blink; bottom-left subtly curious eyebrows eyes open mouth closed; bottom-right friendly speaking with a slightly open natural fox mouth. Do not change head tilt between expressions. Small controlled facial changes, not four different foxes. No exaggerated grin or human teeth. Paint authentic watercolor shapes rather than photo-real fur.
Use a perfectly uniform pure white background with no shadows, paper background texture, decorative marks, text, labels, speech bubbles, borders, UI, accessories, or other characters. Background will be removed separately. Keep light fur distinct from the background. This is a reusable expression sheet, not a scene.
guide.processing: SAM cutouts, local translation to common upper/right silhouette anchors, then 400px export. Decorative expression switching, not phoneme lip sync.
